Notes: Year Established basis: annexation of Dora to the Hasmonean (Jewish) kingdom by Alexander Jannaeus, c. 100 BCE (late 2nd c. BCE; date approximate). Catholic Encyclopedia: Dora passed to the tyrant [Zoilus], 'at whose death it was added by Alexander Jammaeus to his Kingdom of Judea'. This is political control, not a documented Jewish resident community; no source found gives Jewish settlers or a count. Earlier events not used as rows: Israelite period (Dor governed under Solomon by Ben-Abinadab, 1 Kgs 4:11) is pre-586 and not a documented Judahite community; Persian period Dor was a Sidonian possession (Eshmunazar inscription); in 139/138 BCE Antiochus VII besieged Tryphon in Dor, with Simon the Hasmonean sending 2000 troops (1 Macc 15) - a siege, not Jewish residence.

c. 100 or 99 BCE: excavator Andrew Stewart (UC Berkeley, Tel Dor) interprets the dismantling of a Hellenistic Greek temple at Dor as 'a revival of Jewish traditionalism at Dor that occurred briefly in 100 or 99 B.C., when the Jewish king, Alexander Jannaeus, took control of the city', part of a Hasmonean campaign against pagan shrines; the release adds the city 'never stayed long in Jewish hands'. Single excavator's interpretation (later BU seminar by S.R. Martin stresses continuous occupation at Dor in the late 2nd-early 1st c. BCE). No resident Jewish community or numbers documented.

Event: Pompey's settlement (63 BCE) removed Dora from Jewish rule. Josephus, Antiquities 14.4.4 (14.75-76): Pompey restored cities 'to their own inhabitants', including 'of the maritime cities, Gaza, and Joppa, and Dora, and Strato's Tower', and attached them to Syria. End of Hasmonean control; the source does not say whether any Jews lived there, so Population blank (not 0).

c. 57-55 BCE (Gabinius proconsul of Syria; date approximate): Josephus, Antiquities 14.5.3 (14.88): under Gabinius 'were rebuilt Samaria, Ashdod, Scythopolis, Anthedon, Raphia, and Dora' - restoration of the gentile city after the period of Hasmonean rule (the Catholic Encyclopedia reads this as Dora having 'suffered much from the Jews'). Event; no Jewish population data.

c. 41-42 CE (reign of Agrippa I; Claudius' edict of 41; Publius Petronius legate of Syria 39-42): Josephus, Antiquities 19.6.3 (19.300-311): young Greeks of Dora placed a statue of Claudius in the synagogue of the Jews; Agrippa I complained and Petronius ordered the magistrates of Dora to hand over the culprits, affirming the Jews' right to their customs and to equal civic standing (synpoliteuesthai). CIIP (Ameling et al.) concludes Dor 'at the time was a mixed town with city status and enough Jews to maintain a building for their synagogue' - an organized Jewish community with a synagogue; no count. CIIP adds: 'Thereafter there is no evidence for the presence of Jews in the town.' (Hostages held at Dora by Cestius Gallus in 66 CE were from Sepphoris - Josephus, Life 30-31 - not Dor residents.)
